subject: Multiple mediation analysis with dichotomous outcome

messages.author: af8612a18710fff4
messages.subject: Multiple mediation analysis with dichotomous outcome
parts:
Dear all,

I want to identify mediators (all continuous) for the association between independent variable childhood trauma (a continuous predictor coded as 'ZACTISUM') and the dependent variable suicide ideation (a dichotomous variable coded as 'suic_groups_M2fil_aR' -> absent = 0 and present = 1) using Lavaan in R. Note that I also want to correct for sex (a dichotomous variable coded as 'SEX') and age (a continuous variable coded as 'ZAge_per10years').

I am trying to run a multiple mediation model with 9 potential mediators to see which mediators are the main drivers in this association. Unfortunately I do not have many people in my current environment with knowledge of running mediation using Lavaan, so I'm hoping that someone could tell me if my script is correct (see script below) to answer my question. Also, I am wondering I am able to run multiple imputation in combination with the script below. Thank you kindly for your help!

multipleMediation<-'
suic_groups_M2fil_aR ~ b1*Zamasterc + b2*Zaneurot + b3*Zaextrave + b4*ZHOP_R + b5*Zlog_ALAGG + b6*Zabmi + b7*ZaIRSsum + b8*ZCPI_SUM + b9*Zalonelsc + c*ZACTISUM + ZAge_per10years + SEX
Zamasterc ~ a1*ZACTISUM + ZAge_per10years + SEX
Zaneurot ~ a2*ZACTISUM + ZAge_per10years + SEX
Zaextrave ~ a3*ZACTISUM + ZAge_per10years + SEX
ZHOP_R ~ a4*ZACTISUM + ZAge_per10years + SEX
Zlog_ALAGG ~ a5*ZACTISUM + ZAge_per10years + SEX
Zabmi ~ a6*ZACTISUM + ZAge_per10years + SEX
ZaIRSsum ~ a7*ZACTISUM + ZAge_per10years + SEX
ZCPI_SUM ~ a8*ZACTISUM + ZAge_per10years + SEX
Zalonelsc ~ a9*ZACTISUM + ZAge_per10years + SEX
indirect1 :=a1*b1
indirect2 :=a2*b2
indirect3 :=a3*b3
indirect4 :=a4*b4
indirect5 :=a5*b5
indirect6 :=a6*b6
indirect7 :=a7*b7
indirect8 :=a8*b8
indirect9 :=a9*b9
total :=c + (a1 * b1) + (a2*b2) + (a3*b3) + (a4*b4) + (a5*b5) + (a6*b6) + (a7*b7) + (a8*b8) + (a9*b9)
'
fit <- sem(model = simpleMediation, data = MEDSISA, se= "bootstrap", bootstrap = 5000, ordered = c("suic_groups_M2fil_aR"), estimator = "DWLS", missing = "pairwise")
summary(fit, standardized = TRUE, fit.measures = TRUE, ci = TRUE)

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: Multiple mediation analysis with dichotomous outcome
parts:
Jasper,
This is an interesting aspect of implicit threshold models.  Here is the strategy that I would otherwise follow to investigate that question:

lavaanify(multipleMediation) # list parameters
foo <- sem(multipleMediation, do.fit=FALSE, ordered = c("suic_groups_M2fil_aR"))
lavInspect(foo, what='free') # fixed parameters appear as zero
lavInspect(foo, what='start') # start values of parameters

However, this can be misleading with implicit threshold models because the code that auto-generates the threshold model is apparently not triggered this way.  So, with an implicit threshold model, it seems a better strategy to proceed as follows.

bar <- simulateData(model=multipleMediation, ordered = c("suic_groups_M2fil_aR")) 
str(bar)# ordered variable simulated as continuous
summary(bar[,1]) # See distribution
bar[,1] <- cut(bar[,1], breaks=2) # dichotomize ordered variable
baz <- sem(multipleMediation, data=bar, ordered = c("suic_groups_M2fil_aR")) # fit model
summary(baz)
lavInspect(baz, what='free')
lavInspect(baz, what='start')

Here you can see that the threshold model has been implemented as intended.

Here are a few minor things that caught my eye:
1.  You used a different model in your fit from the one you defined.
2.  You can make the total calculation more readable by replacing the products with the  previously defined indirect# parameters.  This will produce the same result.

total := c + indirect1 + indirect2 ...

3. If you desired, you could also define a parameter as the sum of the indirect effects omitting c to obtain inferential statistics for that.  Just be aware that effects in opposite directions can cancel one another out.  A chi-square difference test might offer a more accurate omnibus test in any event.

Keith

I appreciate your thoughts!
Kind regards,

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: Multiple mediation analysis with dichotomous outcome
parts:
Jasper,
I understood your question to be whether your script correctly specified the intended model.  I view that as an important question that everyone should ask and answer as part of any analysis.  So, we need a practical method to answer this question on a routine basis.  The first patch of code illustrates how I address the question as part of my typical work flow.  However, I am somewhat idiosyncratic in that I like to make every parameter explicit in my model specification and always use the lavaan() function rather than the convenience functions to fit models.  Because you were leaving aspects of your model implicit to be filled in by default features, my usual approach did not work for your model.

The second patch of code was meant to suggest a method you could follow to answer the question that would work for the approach that you took to specifying the model.  You will find a list of all the model parameters in a pseudo-output generated by fitting the model to the simulated data.  That can serve the same purpose as the parameter table, checking that all and only the expected parameters are present.  You can also get a sense from the presence of standard errors which are free and which are fixed.  The last two lines supplement this by allowing you to check your model in matrix form.  The first line will display all the free parameters so that you can confirm they are where they should be.  The second line allows you to confirm the values of fixed parameters, which are equal to their start values.  You can ignore the start values for free parameters for purposes of model specification checking.

That procedure should allow you to catch most model specification errors as part of your routine work flow.

Keith
